records.integrity_flag: exif_software = "ACDSee Ultimate 8", exif_datetime 2022-12-17 23:12/23:53 — after the 22:58-23:51 capture window, so the file was batch-processed by an image editor. The identical `depicts` string was a catalogue artefact, not the pixels.
records.profile_basis: eyeballed 2026-08-06: all 24 frames are sun-up exteriors with blue sky and cumulus; none is dawn/dusk/night/overcast, so none can go to exterior_lowlight
records.refile_note: F17/R2C-10: cross-filed to REF-M6 by field, not by copy -- back or three-quarter-rear view of the player character on the gameplay camera, on real ground in real lighting, 40-70% of frame height. `sampling: interval-run` preserved. The file stays in exterior_daylight; REF-M6's population is a query, not a folder.
records.sampling_note: One continuous capture session, 2022-12-17 22:58 to 23:51, twelve locations shot twice each (old-gen then next-gen settings). Not fixed-interval, but not curated for beauty either: every stop in the sweep is present, ugly frames included. Filenames encode seconds since the first frame per the request's run-<slug>-t<s> rule.
records.series_weight_rule: Amendment A15: this is one interval-run series and counts as ONE location. It is downweighted to at most 1/distinct_locations of exterior_daylight band mass for the content-sensitive bands (colour entropy, sky fraction, palette centroid, foliage). It is NOT downweighted for the content-agnostic bands (M4 edge density, M2 local contrast). Its location is Novigrad, which anti-generic/ holds as a NEGATIVE anchor.
records.subject_frame_fraction_basis: by eye at the three-level scale R2C-18 permits. Geralt occupies roughly 45-65% of frame height throughout, which satisfies REF-M6's 40-70% rule -- the first time that clause has been checked against any file.

records.pixel_metrics_note: §5e: refs/morrowind/ is not a fidelity population. A7's measurements are DISPERSION statistics over palette, luminance, edge density, colour entropy, sky fraction and silhouette — computed across this set, not against it.
records.sampling_bias_note: A7's own caveat, carried on every record: Morrowind's screenshot population is skewed toward the picturesque and toward the places players photograph, so any dispersion computed from it is an ESTIMATE FROM A BIASED SAMPLE, not a census. The bias runs against us — a picturesque-skewed sample shows MORE dispersion than the real game — so the floor it yields is harder rather than easier. Record derived statistics as `derived` with this bias stated.
records.vanilla_tests_note: All seven evaluated by eye at full size. V2 is the discriminating test: the vanilla fog wall must close the middle distance. Frames with a crisp horizon behind it were discarded as MGE XE / OpenMW distant land.
